newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse plunges into 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse plunges into 1996 loss.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group said Wednesday that it posted a net loss of 2.59 billion Swiss francs ($1.7 billion) last year due to extraordinary charges of 5.4 billion ($3.65 billion) for restructuring and provisions for bad loans.
The net loss was slightly larger than the 2.1 billion franc ($1.42 billion) loss Credit Suisse forecast last year, when it announced it was changing its method for calculating credit risks.
Swiss banks have been hard hit by the long-running downturn in the Swiss economy and have had to write off billions of francs in bad loans in recent years.
Last year the country's three major banks -- Credit Suisse, Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp. -- changed their method for calculating provisions for loans.
Credit Suisse also embarked on a large-scale restructuring that involved dropping the name of CS Holding from the group and creating four new operational units.
Apart from the extraordinary charges, Credit Suisse's operating results last year improved slightly with pre-tax operating profit rising 3 percent to 2.47 billion francs ($1.67 billion).
Gross earnings from normal banking business rose 17 percent to 12.89 billion ($8,7 billion) with trading income soaring 33 percent to 3.9 billion ($2.63 billion).
